points.response: RD-4 requires the traffic evidence to corroborate the substituted stretch of the optimal route and, on a two-expressway trip, only one incident is on record: F13 is an Accident on Seletar Expressway after Woodlands Avenue 12 Exit reported 17:16, yet F12 shows Tampines Expressway at band 4 (30–39 km/h) during the very window 17:17–18:06 with no incident at all, and F3 shows the detour ran 6.56 km where the optimal route covers 1.64 km at up to 1911 m off-route, well beyond a lane-2 obstruction on the corridor.

RD-4(b) only corroborates when the optimal route is at band 1 or 2 (0–19 km/h), but F11 shows Seletar Expressway at band 5 (40–49 km/h) and F12 shows Tampines Expressway at band 4 (30–39 km/h) — both flowing traffic — so F13 plus a band-5 reading undercuts rather than supports 'reasonable cause', and RD-4(b) cannot exempt a segment on its own in any event.

F3 identifies exactly one off-route segment that no RD-4 exemption reaches, so under RD-2 the metered refund is the detour's extra mileage at this trip's per-km rate: 4.92 km × ($31.37 ÷ 22.25 km = $1.4099) ≈ $6.94, which F4's billed excess of $7.19 for 5.10 km confirms is real money that entered the fare.

We accept that consent is not the operative question here — the rider's case rests on the absence of any RD-4 exemption, not on the absence of agreement (the record in F7, F8, F9 shows no message from the rider about the route at all).

F10 says only that there was 'an accident' and 'lanes were blocked'; the system record F13 says the accident was reported at 17:16 and warned 'Avoid lane 2' — a lane-2 warning, not a closure — and a post-trip statement that contradicts the system record on severity loses to it, while F11's band 5 confirms the expressway kept moving at 40–49 km/h.

We do not contest FARE-1: F6 shows waiting $0.00 and F5 shows no surge, but this is a metered RydeTAXI trip, so the excess 4.92 km of F3 is billed through the distance component ($31.37 for 22.25 km, F6) and is refunded under RD-2, not FARE-1.
We agree no SAFE clause is engaged: F7 and F8 contain only an arrival note and an ETA, and F10 contains no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so we also do not ask for escalation.
The flag_account request is only ancillary: our primary case is the $6.94 RD-2 refund, and if the judge reads F16 as showing no prior route-specific violation we will not press the flag.

C1 is conceded as far as the track goes: F3 does show a 17:38–17:49 segment adding 4.92 km and straying up to 1911 m off the optimal route, but RD-1 does not make such a segment a violation by itself — it is only unexempted once RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 review fails, which is where this case is decided.
